content.title: About
content.content: An alcoholic malt beverage is a low‑alcohol drink produced by fermenting barley malt. It has a sweet‑caramel flavor, a subtle bitterness, and typically contains 0.5–5 % alcohol by volume.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Malt drinks originated in medieval Europe as an inexpensive way to produce alcohol.
In many countries they are called “malt” or “malt ale”.
Malt beverage is often used as a base for cocktails and mixed drinks.
Unlike beer, malt drinks usually lack hops, giving them a smoother, sweeter taste.
They can be non‑alcoholic or lightly alcoholic, making them popular for those seeking a mild buzz.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Malt beverages contain B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: They provide magnesium, phosphorus and potassium, which help muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Moderate alcohol content
items.content: Small amounts may promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Alcohol effects
items.content: Even low alcohol levels can lead to dependence and negatively affect liver health with regular consumption.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Malt drinks often contain significant sugar, contributing to weight gain and dental caries.

items.title: Barley/gluten allergy
items.content: People allergic to barley or gluten may experience reactions.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve chilled, straight or as part of cocktails. It is commonly enjoyed over ice with a slice of lemon or lime for a refreshing twist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a cool, dark place with the container tightly sealed. After opening, store in the refrigerator and consume within 3–5 days.
